cues.en: Mike: I am really excited about this section of the course.
cues.zh: Mike：我對這一章真的很興奮。

cues.en: This is the section where we transition from talking about descriptive statistics and data visualization into inferential statistics.
cues.zh: 在這一章，會從敘述統計和資料視覺化，轉向推論統計。

cues.en: And I guess that you'll probably enrolled in this course because you're most interested in inferential statistics.
cues.zh: 我猜你報名這門課，可能就是因為對推論統計最有興趣。

cues.en: Well, inferential statistics is really all about probability.
cues.zh: 而推論統計，其實完全圍繞著機率。

cues.en: It's about computing probabilities, interpreting probabilities, and translating probabilities into real, tangible, experimental results.
cues.zh: 包括計算機率、解讀機率，以及把機率轉換成真實、具體的實驗結果。

cues.en: Okay, and so I'm gonna kick things off in this video by giving a definition of probability.
cues.zh: 所以這部影片會先給機率下一個定義，作為開場。

cues.en: I'll talk a little bit about misinterpretations of probability and about why probability is an important topic.
cues.zh: 也會稍微談談對機率的誤解，以及為什麼機率是重要主題。

cues.en: There's a lot more details to know about probability and how probability differs from proportion and odds and all sorts of things.
cues.zh: 關於機率，以及它和比例、勝算等等有何不同，還有很多細節。

cues.en: You're gonna learn more about all these details in the rest of this section.
cues.zh: 這一章剩下的內容會介紹更多。

cues.en: So let's dive right in.
cues.zh: 直接開始吧。

cues.en: Now, I don't typically quote directly from websites on the internet, but I happen to find this passage on Wikipedia and I thought it was actually quite good.
cues.zh: 我平常不太直接引用網路上的網站內容，但剛好在維基百科找到這段，覺得寫得很好。

cues.en: So I just decided to literally just paste this in verbatim.
cues.zh: 所以就決定逐字貼上。

cues.en: And this yellow stuff is my addition here.
cues.zh: 黃色部分是我加上的。

cues.en: So according to Wikipedia, "Probability is a numerical description of how likely an event is to occur
cues.zh: 根據維基百科，「機率是以數值描述事件發生的可能性，

cues.en: or how likely it is that a proposition is true.
cues.zh: 或某個命題為真的可能性。

cues.en: Probability is a number between zero and one, where, roughly speaking, zero indicates impossibility and one indicates certainty."
cues.zh: 機率是介於 0 和 1 的數字，粗略來說，0 表示不可能，1 表示確定。」

cues.en: And I added here that the sum of all probabilities in a set must sum to one.
cues.zh: 我在這裡補充，一組所有機率的總和必須為 1。

cues.en: So the total sum of all the probabilities for any possible outcome has to sum to one.
cues.zh: 也就是所有可能結果的機率，合計必須為 1。

cues.en: To give you an example of a statement that involves probability, I'm going to give you a statement and I'm gonna give three different interpretations
cues.zh: 接著用一個包含機率的陳述當例子。我會提出一句話，再給出三種不同解讀，

cues.en: and then I'm going to give you the opportunity to decide which interpretation you think is the correct one.
cues.zh: 讓你有機會決定，哪一種才是正確的。

cues.en: So here's the statement.
cues.zh: 陳述如下。

cues.en: There is a 20% probability of rain today.
cues.zh: 今天下雨的機率是 20%。

cues.en: So what is the proper interpretation of this statement?
cues.zh: 這句話的正確解讀是什麼？

cues.en: It could be that it will rain for 20% of the day, which numerically turns out to be 4.8 hours.
cues.zh: 可能是今天有 20% 的時間會下雨，算起來是 4.8 小時。

cues.en: Or it could be that there is a one in five chance that it will rain today, or it could be, we can be 20% confident
cues.zh: 也可能是今天有五分之一的機會下雨，或是我們有 20% 的信心，

cues.en: that it will rain today.
cues.zh: 認為今天會下雨。

cues.en: So three different interpretations of this statement.
cues.zh: 同一句話，有三種不同解讀。

cues.en: If you want some time to think about this, feel free to pause the video before I go through the answers.
cues.zh: 如果想花點時間思考，可以在我解答前暫停影片。

cues.en: Okay, so it turns out that interpretation one is not correct.
cues.zh: 好，第一種解讀不正確。

cues.en: This is actually the key difference between probability and proportion.
cues.zh: 這其實就是機率和比例的關鍵差異。

cues.en: If I had said, "20% proportional of today is going to be rain," then this statement would've been correct.
cues.zh: 如果我說「今天有 20% 的時間會下雨」，那這個陳述才正確。

cues.en: Okay, so you'll learn more about the difference between probability and proportion in the next video.
cues.zh: 下一部影片會進一步介紹機率和比例的差異。

cues.en: So interpretation two was that there is a one in five chance that it will rain, and this turns out to be the correct answer.
cues.zh: 第二種解讀，是今天有五分之一的機會下雨，這才是正確答案。

cues.en: So if this was your answer as well, then congrats, you've correctly interpreted probability in this statement.
cues.zh: 如果你也選這個，恭喜，你正確解讀了這句話中的機率。

cues.en: And this one is also wrong.
cues.zh: 這一種也錯了。

cues.en: Now, this one gets a little bit tricky, this interpretation three is that we can be 20% confident that it will rain today.
cues.zh: 第三種解讀有點微妙：我們有 20% 的信心，認為今天會下雨。

cues.en: Now the thing is, that what this statement actually means is that if we could repeat the exact conditions of today, let's say, you know,
cues.zh: 問題是，這句話實際上應該表示，如果能重複今天完全相同的條件，假設

cues.en: last night at midnight we branched off our universe and we created a hundred thousand different universes that we're all starting at the same initial conditions.
cues.zh: 昨晚午夜把宇宙分岔，建立十萬個初始條件完全相同的不同宇宙。

cues.en: So we have some like quantum, other worlds happening here, some parallel universes.
cues.zh: 有點像量子多世界，一些平行宇宙。

cues.en: Then, we can expect that in 20% of those, you know, other parallel universes, it's going to rain today.
cues.zh: 那麼可以預期，在其中 20% 的平行宇宙中，今天會下雨。

cues.en: Now, that may seem like it's very similar to interpretation three, but it's actually different.
cues.zh: 這看起來可能和第三種解讀很像，但其實不同。

cues.en: This says we can be 20% confident that it will rain today.
cues.zh: 第三種說的是，有 20% 的信心認為今天會下雨。

cues.en: Now, confidence is different from probability.
cues.zh: 但信心和機率不同。

cues.en: We could be highly confident about our estimate of 20%, or we could be not at all confident about our estimate of 20%.
cues.zh: 我們可以對 20% 這個估計非常有信心，也可以完全沒有信心。

cues.en: So we could say, for example, that we can attach a confidence interval of 19% to 21%.
cues.zh: 例如，可以附上一個從 19% 到 21% 的信賴區間。

cues.en: So this would mean that we are really, really confident that there is a 20% chance of rain today.
cues.zh: 這表示，我們非常非常有信心，今天下雨的機率是 20%。

cues.en: Maybe that's because you know, we have a really, really detailed weather model and that's what it predicts.
cues.zh: 也許因為有非常詳細的天氣模型，而模型就是這樣預測。

cues.en: Or you know, we could be very unconfident, you know, we could lack confidence in our estimate.
cues.zh: 或者，可能很沒信心，對自己的估計缺乏信心。

cues.en: That would be, for example, if we're not using a detailed mathematical climate model, and, you know, let's say I just said, "Well, you know, it tends to rain once a week
cues.zh: 例如，不是使用詳細的數學氣候模型，而只是我說：「過去兩個月，

cues.en: for the past two months.
cues.zh: 大概每週會下雨一次。

cues.en: So I think there's about a 20% chance of rain."
cues.zh: 所以我認為下雨機率約為 20%。」

cues.en: I'm not gonna be very confident even though I'm giving the same answer.
cues.zh: 即使給出相同答案，我也不會很有信心。

cues.en: Okay, so this is really the correct interpretation.
cues.zh: 所以這才是真正正確的解讀。

cues.en: If we could repeat the exact experiment of today, a very large number of times, then we can expect that on 20% of those days it will be raining.
cues.zh: 如果能把今天這個完全相同的實驗重複非常多次，可以預期其中 20% 的日子會下雨。

cues.en: 20% of those experiments will see rain.
cues.zh: 20% 的實驗會觀察到雨。

cues.en: I will give you many, many more examples and discussion points of the correct interpretations of probability.
cues.zh: 我還會提供很多很多例子與討論，說明如何正確解讀機率。

cues.en: So if this still seems a little mysterious, then don't worry, there's gonna be more opportunities to get this right.
cues.zh: 所以如果現在仍覺得有點神祕，不用擔心，之後還有更多機會弄懂。

cues.en: All right, here is three examples of probabilities that you often come across in day-to-day life.
cues.zh: 好，這裡有三個日常生活常見的機率例子。

cues.en: So we have you flip a coin and the probability of it landing heads is 0.5, assuming it's a fair coin.
cues.zh: 擲硬幣，假設是公平硬幣，正面朝上的機率為 0.5。

cues.en: Here we roll a die and the probability of getting a three is one in six because there are six sides.
cues.zh: 擲骰子，因為有六面，出現 3 的機率是六分之一。

cues.en: So one in six corresponds to 16 and two-thirds percent.
cues.zh: 六分之一對應 16 又三分之二%。

cues.en: So we have a almost 17% chance of rolling a three.
cues.zh: 所以擲出 3 的機率接近 17%。

cues.en: And here, we have a queen of hearts.
cues.zh: 這裡則是一張紅心 Q。

cues.en: So the question is, what is the probability of choosing the queen of hearts randomly from a deck of cards?
cues.zh: 問題是，從一副牌隨機抽到紅心 Q 的機率是多少？

cues.en: Well, there's one queen of hearts and there's 52 cards.
cues.zh: 只有一張紅心 Q，而總共有 52 張牌。

cues.en: So that gives us a probability of almost 2%, bit under 2%.
cues.zh: 所以機率接近 2%，略低於 2%。

cues.en: By the way, you'll notice that here I wrote 0.5, and here I wrote numbers in percent.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，你會注意到，這裡寫 0.5，這裡則用百分比。

cues.en: So there's no percent sign here.
cues.zh: 這裡沒有百分號。

cues.en: So this is not 0.5%, which would be one half of a percent.
cues.zh: 所以不是 0.5%，那會是百分之一的一半。

cues.en: You can list probabilities either between zero and one or between zero and 100.
cues.zh: 機率可以寫成 0 到 1 之間的數字，也可以寫成 0 到 100 之間。

cues.en: And if you're going up to 100, then it's important to use the percent sign there.
cues.zh: 如果寫到 100 的尺度，就務必加上百分號。

cues.en: So why is probability an important topic?
cues.zh: 為什麼機率是重要主題？

cues.en: Well, first of all, so probability theory was developed by many important mathematicians over the past few centuries, but it's largely attributed to the Bernoulli family.
cues.zh: 首先，機率理論是過去幾個世紀中許多重要數學家共同發展的，但很大程度上歸功於 Bernoulli 家族。

cues.en: There's quite a bunch of these Bernoullis.
cues.zh: Bernoulli 家族有不少人。

cues.en: They were Swiss, I believe, mathematicians, and it was a whole family of them.
cues.zh: 我想他們是瑞士數學家，而且是一整個家族。

cues.en: They were all brilliant mathematicians.
cues.zh: 全都是傑出的數學家。

cues.en: And of course, Bayes, I'm sure you've heard the term Bayes before.
cues.zh: 當然還有 Bayes，相信你聽過 Bayes 這個名字。

cues.en: He's also a a mathematician.
cues.zh: 他也是數學家。

cues.en: And the story goes, I don't know if this is true, but it's something I've heard several times that basically modern statistics
cues.zh: 據說，我不知道是不是真的，但聽過好幾次，現代統計

cues.en: and probability theory came from these mathematicians being hired by rich people to help them make more money when gambling.
cues.zh: 與機率理論，基本上源於富人聘請這些數學家，幫他們在賭博時賺更多錢。

cues.en: Again, I don't know if that's really true. Okay.
cues.zh: 再次說明，我不知道這到底是不是真的。好。

cues.en: Probability theory is central to trying to predict the weather to make insurance predictions, which is called actuarial science.
cues.zh: 機率理論對天氣預測，以及保險預測，也就是精算學，都至關重要。

cues.en: So things about risk, calculating risk, probability is important in medicine, particularly modeling disease spread
cues.zh: 例如風險、風險計算；機率在醫學也很重要，尤其是建立疾病傳播模型，

cues.en: and determining whether particular treatments for a disease or condition are going to be effective.
cues.zh: 以及判斷針對某種疾病或狀況的特定治療是否有效。

cues.en: Probability is central to basically every area of science, physics, chemistry, biology, psychology, geology, you name it.
cues.zh: 機率基本上是所有科學領域的核心，物理、化學、生物、心理、地質，什麼都有。

cues.en: If there's something remotely sciencey involved, then probability is definitely important.
cues.zh: 只要稍微涉及科學，機率肯定很重要。

cues.en: And of course, the new field or emerging fields of machine learning, deep learning, AI, all these stuff is really just about putting probability to work to make predictions.
cues.zh: 當然，機器學習、深度學習、AI 這些新興領域，基本上也都是讓機率發揮作用，做出預測。

cues.en: So here's a question.
cues.zh: 這裡有個問題。

cues.en: When do we need probability?
cues.zh: 什麼時候需要機率？

cues.en: What are the situations where we need probability theory?
cues.zh: 哪些情況需要機率理論？

cues.en: We need to compute and interpret probabilities versus when we don't need probabilities.
cues.zh: 什麼時候需要計算和解讀機率，什麼時候不需要？

cues.en: So if you like, you can pause the video here and see if you can come up with an answer.
cues.zh: 如果願意，可以暫停影片，想想答案。

cues.en: When do we need probability?
cues.zh: 什麼時候需要機率？

cues.en: Well, the answer is according to me, and other people, (chuckles) I'm sure it's not just only my opinion.
cues.zh: 答案是，根據我，以及其他人的看法，〔笑〕我相信不只是我個人的意見，

cues.en: We need probability when there is uncertainty about the outcome of an event.
cues.zh: 當事件的結果有不確定性時，就需要機率。

cues.en: So we can also turn this statement around.
cues.zh: 也可以反過來說。

cues.en: When there already is certainty about some event occurring, we actually do not really need probability theory.
cues.zh: 當某個事件是否發生已經確定，其實不太需要機率理論。

cues.en: So we don't always need probability.
cues.zh: 所以不是每次都需要機率。

cues.en: Here's a few examples.
cues.zh: 這裡有幾個例子。

cues.en: Let's say you wanted to know the relative speed of light versus the speed of sound.
cues.zh: 假設想知道，光速和聲速哪個比較快。

cues.en: Well, light is really, really, really, really fast.
cues.zh: 光真的非常非常快。

cues.en: It travels super fast and speed is kind of fast, but it's actually not that fast.
cues.zh: 它傳得超快，而聲音也算快，但其實沒那麼快。

cues.en: Certainly, it's much, much slower.
cues.zh: 肯定慢得多。

cues.en: Sound is much, much slower relative to light.
cues.zh: 相對於光，聲音慢得多。

cues.en: Now, these are known constants.
cues.zh: 這些是已知的常數。

cues.en: The speed of light, of course, is a constant.
cues.zh: 光速當然是常數。

cues.en: The speed of sound can vary depending on the medium and so forth, but we actually don't need probability to determine which is faster light or sound.
cues.zh: 聲速則可能隨介質等等改變，但要判斷光和聲音哪個比較快，其實不需要機率。

cues.en: Okay. Here's another question.
cues.zh: 好，另一個問題。

cues.en: The height of men on average versus the height of women on average.
cues.zh: 男性的平均身高，和女性的平均身高相比。

cues.en: Now, here is something where we need probability theory for, and that's because it is not the case that every single man is taller than every single woman.
cues.zh: 這就需要機率理論，因為並不是每個男性都比每個女性高。

cues.en: You can certainly find any particular woman that's gonna be taller than any particular man.
cues.zh: 確實可以找到比某位男性更高的某位女性。

cues.en: So we don't necessarily know just by wandering around and looking at people, whether men are generally taller than women.
cues.zh: 所以不能只是到處看看人，就一定知道男性通常是否比女性高。

cues.en: So there is some uncertainty.
cues.zh: 這裡有一些不確定性。

cues.en: So here's a case where we definitely need probabilities.
cues.zh: 所以這是確實需要機率的情況。

cues.en: Here's another example.
cues.zh: 再舉一個例子。

cues.en: Whether a test for a disease indicates the presence of the disease.
cues.zh: 疾病檢測是否表示真的有那個疾病。

cues.en: This is a super important application of probability.
cues.zh: 這是機率非常重要的應用。

cues.en: You want to know if you test positive for cancer, you want to know what is the chance that you really have cancer, given that the test was positive.
cues.zh: 如果癌症檢測呈陽性，你會想知道，在陽性的條件下，真正罹患癌症的機率是多少。

cues.en: Now, many medical tests, diagnostic tests, are accurate to, you know, 99.9%, but that still means that they're going to give false positives.
cues.zh: 很多醫療診斷檢測的準確率可達 99.9%，但仍然表示會有偽陽性。

cues.en: They're gonna give incorrect results every once in a while.
cues.zh: 偶爾還是會產生錯誤結果。

cues.en: So we actually need some probability theory to understand the accuracy of these diagnostic tools.
cues.zh: 所以需要一些機率理論，理解這些診斷工具的準確性。

cues.en: And here's a final example, whether a potato will fall to the ground if you drop it.
cues.zh: 最後一個例子，放手讓馬鈴薯掉下去時，它是否會落到地面。

cues.en: I don't know why you would drop a perfectly good potato, maybe it's too hot.
cues.zh: 我不知道為什麼要丟一顆好好的馬鈴薯，也許太燙了。

cues.en: But question is, do we need probability theory to answer this question?
cues.zh: 但問題是，需要機率理論來回答嗎？

cues.en: Here, I would actually argue no.
cues.zh: 這裡我會主張，不需要。

cues.en: The theory of gravity is pretty well mapped out.
cues.zh: 重力理論已經研究得相當清楚。

cues.en: I don't think we need to compute probabilities to predict whether a potato is likely to fall to the ground if you drop it.
cues.zh: 我認為不需要計算機率，來預測放手後馬鈴薯是否可能落到地面。

cues.en: And by the way, if you are considering trying this experiment, if it's a really buttery potato, then, I don't know, drop it on top of a floor that's easy to clean
cues.zh: 順帶一提，如果考慮做這個實驗，而馬鈴薯上又有很多奶油，那我想，請在容易清理的地板上丟，

cues.en: or just don't do this experiment at all.
cues.zh: 或者乾脆不要做這個實驗。

cues.en: All right, so in this video, I gave you an introduction to probability.
cues.zh: 好，這部影片介紹了機率。

cues.en: I defined probability.
cues.zh: 給機率下了定義。

cues.en: I gave you an example of how probabilities can be misinterpreted.
cues.zh: 也舉例說明機率可能如何被誤解。

cues.en: And I hope this sets you up for the rest of this section where I'm going to detail a lot more about probability theory.
cues.zh: 希望這能為本章剩下的內容打好基礎，接下來會更詳細介紹機率理論。
